title: Integer `+ - *`, unary `-` and `**`: wrap at the column's width
description: Integer arithmetic wraps at the operands' width (two's complement, Rust's `wrapping_add`, `wrapping_sub`, `wrapping_mul`, `wrapping_neg`): `Int8` 127 + 1 is -128, `-MIN` is `MIN`. No setting makes it raise or saturate. Polars keeps the width of the operands; a literal takes the column's type.
`**` on integers wraps too (`2 ** 63` is `-2⁶³` in `Int64`); a negative integer exponent raises (`InvalidOperationError`, the exponent is cast to `u32`).
reference: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `negate` with `overflow: ERROR` when the plan omits it (#202); `SILENT` when the plan asks. Polars gives `SILENT` natively; `ERROR` needs a guard, at each width.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `pow_to_uint_dtype`: an exponent literal of 2 to 10 multiplies the column by itself, any other calls `Pow::pow`.
`pow_on_series`: an integer base with an integer exponent, for every width by `with_match_physical_integer_type!`.
num-traits 0.2.19 (Polars's Cargo.lock): `Pow<u32>` for i8, i16, i32, i64 is the primitive `pow`.

notes: Integer `**` with an integer exponent is one generic function, `pow_to_uint_dtype`, instantiated for each width by `with_match_physical_integer_type!`. An exponent literal from 2 to 10 multiplies the column by itself with the `*` kernel, which wraps (`wrapping_mul`, the same macro for i8 to i64); any other exponent calls num-traits's `Pow<u32>`, the primitive `i8::pow` to `i64::pow`. The wheels build with the `dist-release` profile, which inherits `release` and leaves `overflow-checks` off, so the primitive `pow` wraps too. So `Int8`, `Int16` and `Int32` wrap as the `Int64` probe does, and the result keeps the base's type (`pow_dtype`).
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.
